title: Live-patch coordinator and tenant-aware escalation for cross-environment model regressions
creator: Sophie Nguyen
description:
Problem: Recent model rollouts have produced tenant-specific degradations that escape global canary metrics and require coordinated live patches or targeted rollbacks across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket establishes an operational coordinator role, a live-patch playbook, tenant-aware rollback windows, and automated sanity checkpoints to minimize customer-facing downtime during model regressions.

Scope: playbook and runbook for engineers and oncall to perform fast live patches (code + model pin + config change), isolate affected tenant slices, reconcile KV cache mismatches, and coordinate customer communication. Includes templates for notices, required dashboards/alerts, and post-incident actions. Excludes long-term runtime optimizations (separate project).
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: confirm regression signature (latency spike, hallucination rate, token error types) and scope using per-tenant histograms in Console -> Model Health.
2) Isolate: add tenant to a quarantined routing slice (routing policy: tenant-id -> fallback-model), reduce concurrency and disable batching for the slice to limit spread.
3) Snapshot: capture KV cache/embedding cache snapshots and request samples tied to tenant for forensic replay (store in S3 bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/ENG-106534/).

4) Live-patch: coordinate a two-step live patch when possible — apply config-only mitigations (temperature/top_p clamp, disable tools) then apply model pin or hotpatch binary via canary pipeline, target only quarantined slice first.
5) KV reconciliation: after patching, run kvcache-reconcile job to ensure cache keys are compatible; if mismatch, trigger per-tenant cache flush with gracebackoff.
6) Validation: run synthetic prompt set (tenant-specific) and compare generation metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-like proxy and hallucination trigger count) against pre-rollout baseline.
7) Release or Rollback: if validation passes and SLOs restored, expand rollout to original traffic weighting; otherwise, execute targeted rollback and escalate to oncall leads.
8) Customer comms: use templated messages (initial acknowledgment within 30m, mitigation update at 2h, resolution + RCA within 72h).
9) Postmortem: create post-incident ticket linking PRs, metrics, and action items (must include a dedicated safe-deploy test for this tenant slice).
checklist: Pager notified and primary engineer acknowledged
Quarantine routing policy applied to tenant slice
Model pin or hotpatch deployed to slice
Synthetic validation passed or failed recorded
Incident ticket created in ops tracker and linked to customer support thread
monitoring_and_alerts: Per-tenant error rate alert (threshold: >0.5% 5m increase vs baseline)
Model inference OOM or kernel errors
templates_and_links: Customer ack template: 'We've identified unusual behavior in your model requests and are actively mitigating; we'll follow up within 2 hours with next steps.'
risk_and_tradeoffs: Live-patching minimizes customer downtime but risks introducing new regressions — mitigated by slice-only rollout and short validation window.
Flushing tenant KV cache reduces inconsistent outputs but causes temporary latency and cold-cache degradation for affected users.
Targeted rollbacks must consider cross-compatibility between model variants and downstream tokenization/format assumptions.
Private deployments may require manual KMS approvals and longer patch cycles — add extra 1-2 hour window for coordination.
